question: Regarding the battle between the player and Elder Jinchi (金池长老), which of the following statements are correct? 1. The player used Red Tides (变身广智) 2. The player did not use Wandering Wight (幽魂) Spirit (精魄) 3. After the battle ended, the player obtained the Fire Shield (避火罩) 4. The player used Cloud Step (聚形散气)

rollouts.answer: Correct statements: 3 and 4 (item1 judged false, item2 judged false-statement/true-usage, item4 judged true)

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa(5880-6000) asked specifically about Red Tides answered 'No' transformation, missing that the transformation actually happens at ~6019.5-6021 which was outside this window
clip_qa(5880-6120) asked about Wandering Wight answered 'Yes... around 6019.5-6024.5' -- this is actually the Red Tides transformation window, mislabeled as Wandering Wight
clip_qa(5880-6120) asked about Cloud Step answered 'Yes ... 6019.4-6020.0' -- again the same single blue-gray-smoke event, now labeled Cloud Step

rollouts.failure_point: Same ~6019.5-6021s blue-gray-smoke-to-fire transformation event was probed with three separate leading single-ability questions and answered 'yes'/'no' inconsistently for each; the true Red Tides transformation was missed (called 'no transformation') because the query window (5880-6000) ended just before the event, and the actual event was instead mislabeled as Wandering Wight and Cloud Step. The earlier, real Wandering Wight event (~5889-5890) was never probed at all.
rollouts.evidence_checked: frame extraction at 5889-5891 and 6019.5-6021 confirms a dark large hunched form fighting at 5889-5890 (true Wandering Wight) and a distinct blue-gray-smoke-to-fiery-orange transformation at 6019.5-6020.5 (true Red Tides); rollout 0 never sampled near 5889 and conflated the 6020s event across two different ability labels.

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa(5880-5970) for Red Tides answered 'no activation, normal monkey form' -- missed because the actual transformation is at 6019.5-6021, outside this window
clip_qa(5970-6060) for Cloud Step said 'no clear Cloud Step, but noted brief blue smoke' -- the same real transformation event, seen but explicitly ruled out as Cloud Step
clip_qa(6060-6150) said 'player uses Cloud Step near the end, not Red Tides' -- a further, different reading of a nearby moment
clip_qa(5880-6090) for Wandering Wight answered 'No... only transformation seen is Guangzhi' despite the real Wandering Wight event at ~5889-5890 falling inside this exact window

rollouts.failure_point: Windowed decomposition of the single battle interval into three separate clip_qa calls, each asked about a different ability, produced mutually inconsistent per-window verdicts (no Red Tides in window 1, no clear Cloud Step in window 2, Cloud Step near the end in window 3); the final written answer then asserted Red Tides was seen at 6020s anyway, contradicting its own clip_qa evidence, and also asserted no Wandering Wight despite that event lying inside a probed window -- suggesting synthesis error on top of noisy visual evidence.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Same frame evidence as rollout 0 shows a genuine Wandering Wight event at 5889-5890 inside the window rollout 1 explicitly queried (5880-6090) yet reported 'No'.

rollouts.answer: 1, 3, 4 correct; 2 incorrect (i.e. player did use Wandering Wight)

decisive_steps.what_happened: single clip_qa call over the full 5880-6120 window asked a compound question about Red Tides, Wandering Wight and Cloud Step together, answered 'Yes for two of the three (Red Tides ~6020, Cloud Step ~6019.4-6020.0), and no for Wandering Wight' -- missing the real Wandering Wight event at 5889-5890 entirely and again mislabeling the transformation-transition smoke as a separate Cloud Step activation

rollouts.failure_point: Used only one broad, compound-question clip_qa call for the whole battle instead of multiple narrower windows/questions, giving the sub-agent less chance to notice the early (5889-5890) Wandering Wight event, and it split the single 6019.5-6021 transformation event into two separate 'yes' answers (Red Tides and Cloud Step). The final written answer then asserted item 2 ('did not use Wandering Wight') was TRUE, i.e. the player never used it -- directly contradicted by the real footage -- making this the worst-covered rollout of the five.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Same frame evidence: genuine Wandering Wight event visible at 5889-5890 was never surfaced by this rollout's single wide-window clip_qa call.

rollouts.answer: 1, 3, 4 correct; 2 incorrect (i.e. player did use Wandering Wight, around 6019.5-6020.5)

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa(5880-6120) for Wandering Wight/spirit transformation answered 'Yes, ... 6019.5-6021.5' -- the identical time window as the Red Tides answer above
clip_qa(5880-6120) for Cloud Step answered 'Yes, ~6019.5-6020.0, dense blue-gray cloud' -- again the same single event

rollouts.failure_point: The exact same 6019.5-6021.5s single transformation event was independently confirmed 'Yes' to three separate leading questions (is this Red Tides? is this Wandering Wight? is this Cloud Step?), showing the visual sub-agent will agree with whichever specific ability is named for an ambiguous smoke effect rather than distinguishing them. The final answer happened to mark item 2 as false (matching the reference) but for the wrong reason -- it never found or used the real, earlier Wandering Wight event at 5889-5890 -- and it still wrongly kept item 4 (Cloud Step) as true.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Same frames confirm 6019.5-6021.5 is the Red Tides transition only; the true Wandering Wight moment is 5889-5890, which this rollout's clip_qa windows (all 5880-6120) technically covered but the sub-agent's answer text never mentions or localizes it there.

db_evidence.notes: The text memory layers (episodes, semantic_triples, topic_facts, visual_clips, object_states) contain no mention at all of Red Tides, Wandering Wight, or Cloud Step within the 5876-6165s battle window; the only textual facts recoverable by SQL/semantic search are the boss identity, dialogue lines, and the Fire Shield (辟火罩) item popup at 6150-6180s. All information about which of the three abilities the player used is only visible in raw video frames, which is why every rollout had to fall back to clip_qa, and why all rollouts got item 3 (Fire Shield) right but were inconsistent on items 1/2/4.

root_causes: The three abilities (Red Tides transformation start, Wandering Wight transformation, and a possible Cloud Step) all begin with a visually similar blue-gray smoke/cloud effect enveloping the player; the visual sub-agent (clip_qa) cannot reliably distinguish between them from sampled frames and tends to answer 'Yes' to whatever specific ability name is asked about for that same ambiguous moment (confirmed directly in rollouts 2 and 4, where the identical 6019.5-6021s window was independently labeled as Red Tides, Wandering Wight, and Cloud Step in three separate single-ability questions)
There is no textual/DB evidence at all for these three ability names in the battle window, so the agents had no way to cross-check or override the visual sub-agent's inconsistent readings

The real, distinct Wandering Wight event occurs earlier (~5889-5890s, a visually different dark/black large form) than the ambiguous 6019.5-6021s smoke event; rollouts that queried the whole span with a single broad or leading question (rollouts 1 and 3) missed this early event, while rollouts that used finer, earlier windows (rollout 2) or asked about it directly (rollout 0) found it

Cloud Step (statement 4, reference-false) was marked true in all 5 rollouts, because the same 6019.5-6020s smoke transition into the Red Tides fire form was repeatedly reread as a separate Cloud Step activation -- no rollout ever produced visual evidence of a genuinely distinct Cloud Step event
what_worked: Every rollout correctly retrieved and confirmed the Fire Shield (辟火罩) item popup at ~6150-6180s via a semantic_triples/topic_facts hit plus a confirming clip_qa call, since this fact IS present in the text memory layer

Rollout 2, which used the most, narrowest (~60s) clip_qa windows starting right at the battle's opening (5880-5940), was the only rollout to correctly locate and describe the true early Wandering Wight event at 5889-5890
transferable_lessons: When a question distinguishes between several similarly-effected in-game abilities (e.g. multiple transformations that all start with a smoke/cloud VFX), do not ask the visual sub-agent one leading yes/no question per ability over the same time window -- it will tend to agree with whichever ability is named. Instead ask one open, non-leading question per time window ('what ability, if any, does the player use here, and what happens immediately after the effect clears') and use the resulting visual outcome (fire form vs a large dark creature form vs nothing) to disambiguate

Sample clip_qa windows starting at the very beginning of the cited clue interval, not just around the region where the semantic/SQL search happened to surface hits -- the earliest, most visually distinct event (Wandering Wight at 5889-5890) was missed by rollouts that only probed windows further into the fight or asked one compound question for the whole span

When two 'abilities' are reported at nearly the same timestamp by different clip_qa calls, treat that as a red flag for the same underlying visual event being mislabeled twice, and re-verify with a single broader/neutral question rather than accepting both as independently true

For hallucination-detection questions with 4 statements, submitting an answer where 3-4 statements are marked true is suspicious for this style of question (typically only some subset is genuinely correct) -- worth a final sanity pass asking the visual sub-agent to directly confirm/deny each claimed positive against a fresh, unbiased viewing before submitting
open_questions: Whether a true 'Cloud Step' (聚形散气) ability exists visually anywhere else in this fight and was simply never sampled by any of the 5 rollouts, or whether it genuinely never occurs and the reference answer's exclusion of item 4 is fully correct -- not exhaustively checked beyond the frames around 6019.5-6021 and 6075

Exact wording/translation mapping between the abilities named in the question (Red Tides/变身广智, Wandering Wight/幽魂, Cloud Step/聚形散气) and the in-game HUD ability names actually shown in the frames (e.g. '皎月', '定身法') was not independently verified against an external game reference
